messages:
maya: heads-up — noticed big client heap growth right after we flipped the telemetry-proxy canary. charts become janky and the metrics pane sometimes freezes for ~5-10s. attaching flamechart in a sec but wanted to flag.
ian: saw the same on staging. LCP for metrics tiles spiked from ~650ms to ~2.1s. memory graphs show sustained growth per route.
sam: any recent frontend deps? we shipped telemetry-client 2.4.0 yesterday in the canary.
maya: yep that one. quick snapshot from chrome: `JS heap used ~1.4GB` at peak, then GC thrash. stack traces point to chart-worker message queue growing (not clearing).
jess: could be the telemetry proxy attaching more tags / event shapes and telemetry-client serializing bigger objects, which get handed off to workers and kept alive.
maya: here's a tiny repro snippet from console where we saw retained closures:
```)window.telemetry.emit('render_complete', {route: '/metrics', tiles: tilesSnapshot, ctx: largeCtx});
// largeCtx contains nested arrays of series + sampler state
```
sam: we also enabled prefix prefetching in the same deploy for canary routes. wonder if prefetch + telemetry = double-hold on large payloads.
velma: can we confirm whether the worker message uses structuredClone or postMessage(copy) pattern? structuredClone might keep references alive until GC differently.
ian: looks like we `postMessage({type:'render', payload: bigArray})` into worker. worker does an `onmessage` and then pushes to a local queue for processing. queue never drains if processing is slower than incoming rate.
jess: two hypotheses: (1) telemetry increases payload size so queue backlog forms; (2) telemetry-client introduced a bug where it wraps payloads with extra metadata references preventing GC. both are plausible.
maya: mitigation idea: throttle telemetry emission on canary routes (sample down to 10%) and revert prefetch for the canary. that should reduce pressure.
sam: agree. we should patch config in rollout to set `telemetry.sample_rate=0.1` and `prefetch.enabled=false` for canary flag.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback candidate or patch config. Approve with `/deploy patch canary-config telemetry-sample=0.1 prefetch=false`.
ian: quick tracer check — the console's telemetry pipeline adds a `largeCtx` by default for legacy routes. we can make the pipeline `stripLargeCtx` behind a feature flag so serverside and client agree.
velma: also suggest adding a guard in the worker: if queue length > 50 drop oldest messages and increment metric `worker.queue_drop`. better than OOM.
jess: agreed. small change in worker handler + metrics and config tweak for canary. who wants to own the quickfix?
maya: I can ship the canary config toggle and worker queue guard. will follow up with a small smoke job to exercise heavy charts.
sam: i'll open a PR to make telemetry-client opt-in for fullContext and add a unit test around serialization.
ian: timeline — if maya patches canary config in next 30m we can watch staging for regressions, then promote. otherwise we rollback telemetry-proxy.
jess: also notify product infra that console UX is impaired for canary users so they don't escalate.
maya: copying notes: patching now, will post results in ~20m. thanks. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy started for canary-config patch by maya — job id 78921.
maya: update 18m — staging memory still a bit high but not spiking. charts responsive. pushing to small subset in prod.
sam: nice — opening follow-ups: (1) telemetry-client change; (2) prefetch audit for large payloads; (3) longer-term: move heavy ctx to indexeddb and pass handles only.
velma: add alert: `console.worker.queue_depth > 100` to P1 so we catch before UX regresses.
jess: will add a rollout note in the console runbook.
maya: resolved for now, leaving thread open for the follow-ups.
